title: Sedan
body:
Sedan is a passenger car with a closed body, a separate boot, and seating for four or five across two rows. The sedan was the default family car for most of the twentieth century, valued for comfort, quiet, and a clear separation between passengers and luggage.

Sedans remain a major car type worldwide, even as crossovers have grown, and the form defines the classic image of the automobile.

title: Hatchback
body:
Hatchback is a small or mid-sized car whose rear door lifts to open the whole back of the car, giving flexible cargo space in a short body. Hatchbacks are the standard city and first car in Europe and much of the world, prized for parking ease and practicality.

The hatchback's genius is its versatility: a small car that carries like a much larger one when the rear seats fold.

title: Sports Utility Vehicle
body:
Sports Utility Vehicle is a car built on a high, wagon-like body with raised ground clearance, a large cargo area, and often all-wheel drive. SUVs grew from off-road vehicles into the best-selling car type in many markets, blending family practicality with a commanding driving position.

The SUV's rise reshaped the car industry, moving buyers from sedans and estates into taller, roomier bodies.

title: Pickup Truck
body:
Pickup Truck is a light truck with an enclosed cab and an open cargo bed at the rear, built for work and for leisure hauling. Pickups are the best-selling vehicles in the United States, where models such as the Ford F-Series have led sales for decades.

The pickup is both a work tool and a cultural icon, and its evolution from farm vehicle to family transport is a central story of American motoring.

title: Convertible
body:
Convertible is a car whose roof folds or retracts, giving open-air driving. Convertibles range from small roadsters to grand tourers, and they trade some practicality for the pleasure of driving with the sky overhead.

The convertible is motoring's romantic type, kept alive by enthusiasts even as fixed-roof cars dominate sales.

title: Electric Car
body:
Electric Car is a car driven by one or more electric motors powered by a rechargeable battery, with no exhaust pipe and instant torque. Electric cars are the fastest-growing car type of the twenty-first century, led by models such as the Tesla Model 3 and the Nissan Leaf.

Electric cars are changing the car itself: fewer moving parts, new packaging freedom, and a direct link to renewable electricity.

title: Classic Car: Ford Model T
body:
Classic Car: Ford Model T was produced by Ford from 1908 to 1927, with over fifteen million built, and it put the automobile within reach of ordinary families. The Model T's moving assembly line cut its price year after year and created mass motoring.

The Model T is a public fact of industrial history: the car that turned the automobile from a luxury into a mass product.

title: Supercar
body:
Supercar is a high-performance sports car built for extreme speed, handling, and presence, usually with a mid-mounted engine and exotic materials. Supercars from makers such as Ferrari and Lamborghini are engineering showcases as much as road cars.

The supercar is the car industry's dream type, where cost is secondary to performance and design ambition.
